intro: Your garage door springs handle hundreds of pounds of door weight. When a spring breaks, you often hear a loud bang from the garage. The door will then feel extremely heavy or refuse to lift at all. Broken springs mean your garage door opener is working too hard, or not at all. This creates a safety risk and can damage your opener. We provide expert garage door spring repair for Mount Prospect homes. We offer upfront flat-rate quotes before any work begins. Our technicians arrive with common parts stocked on their trucks. We offer emergency dispatch 24 hours a day, Monday through Saturday. Book online to save 10% on your service.
localContext: Many Mount Prospect homes, especially in areas like Prospect Manor and We-Go Park, were built in the 1950s and 1960s. They often feature original steel garage doors. These doors are typically un-insulated, single-skin panels. During subzero January days, these older doors visibly bow inward under extreme cold. This bending puts extra strain on tracks, hinges, and especially on the torsion and extension springs. Over time, this stress leads to premature spring fatigue and breakage. Even newer homes in Countryside with inadequate doors can face these issues. Regular use in cold weather shortens spring lifespan.

problemSigns.detail: A broken spring often makes a loud noise as it snaps under tension.

problemSigns.sign: Door won't lift or feels heavy
problemSigns.detail: Without spring assistance, your garage door becomes extremely heavy or impossible to open manually or with an opener.
A clear separation or gap in the coils of the torsion spring above the door indicates it is broken.

problemSigns.sign: Door lifts a few inches then stops
problemSigns.detail: This can signal a broken spring, as the opener struggles to lift the full weight.
Loose or slack cables around the pulleys mean the spring system is not under proper tension.
